rules.rule: Play a card by dragging it onto a glowing target or by clicking it and then clicking the target (clicking is the most reliable method); right-click cancels the aim, though inconsistently. The aim arrow with 'LANDS HERE' only appears once a card is selected and previews the result before you commit; aim feedback can be delayed, so wait a moment after clicking. Nudge cards go on nudge buttons and slice cards on slices. Clicking a wheel with no card selected does nothing. Jolt and Fine Tune often default their aim to the enemy wheel, so check the aim readout and click your own wheel to move your needle. Some cards (Fine Tune) may never confirm after many clicks; Space may commit an aimed card, otherwise Undo and try another card.

Undo (Z) is free and unlimited within a turn and refunds cards and RAM, but it stops at a respin or random pick/event. Turns begin with a random spin, so Undo only rewinds back to that spin and is blocked on turns that began with one; plan cards and nudges before queuing. The UNDO button sits bottom right and is easy to miss-click. Use it to safely test a card before sending.

Esc usually opens the pause menu instead of cancelling a card aim (some sessions found Esc did clear a stuck aim, and in the training sim Esc did nothing so use the gear icon); to clear a stuck aim, press Z/Undo first, or right-click, or re-select a card from the hand.

Number keys 1-5 select hand cards and Space sends the turn (works in normal fights; advances some tutorial/loot steps but not 'do it in the fight' steps); hand order shifts between turns so re-read card keys before pressing. Keys only pick the card; aiming still needs a mouse click. A key may do nothing if the card costs more RAM than you have left.

Use Q/E to nudge the active wheel one tick (Q is anticlockwise), W to switch wheels or nudge the target, and R to switch between rings; each turn starts with one free nudge that is spent at 0 (after which the nudge arrow does nothing) and refreshes next turn. Extra nudges cost RAM. One session saw no visible effect from Q/E and had to click the arrow.

The small arrow icons above the wheels are the nudge buttons: nudge cards (Fine Tune, etc.) go on them, not the wheel body, and you can click them directly to use the per-turn free nudge; with no nudge card in hand the free nudge does nothing useful.
Enemy-wheel nudge buttons show no key hint and must be clicked with the mouse.
Nudge effects can resolve late: a Fine Tune that showed no change was applied at turn resolution.

On the loot sheet, Space only lights card 1 and Continue takes the lit card; click the card you want before Continue. Stray number or Space presses can auto-take cards, and Continue stays unresponsive while a firmware pick is pending (try Enter or Skip if clicks are ignored).

Most menu buttons (JACK IN, CONTINUE, node picks, Back to HQ, BACK TO THE GRID, START DEFENSE, tutorial NEXT/FINISH, loot Continue, pause items, Save & quit) show no key and need a mouse click; Enter or Space rarely work there (Enter did confirm a selected route node). Clicking tutorial NEXT/FINISH is more reliable than Space (Space worked in some sessions, was ignored in others).

Event options: if clicking an option does nothing, try the number key (1, 2...); number keys often did nothing (key 1 on a kiosk, key 3 on a terminal did not register), so try both and prefer clicking.
The fight-won banner may show no Continue button and ignore clicks; open the pause menu (Esc or gear) to get out.
Scroll wheel jumps on long setup pages are large at 2.0x text, so scroll in small increments to avoid overshooting the start controls.
Quit to Main Menu is available from the pause menu and saves the run.
The Quit confirm shows a QUIT [A] hint, but pressing A did nothing; click the button.

Before Send It, check the outcome chips (red skull/negative numbers) and damage preview numbers beside each HP bar and hover Send It: they show expected damage to both sides after block, who hits whom and lethal flags. Previews matched actual results in normal fights. Blind sending cost about 12 HP per turn. Send It resolves all needles at once: defensive slices, then offensive slices, then statuses. Enemy HP doesn't change until you send.

If the preview shows a lethal chip on you, do not send; use a card or nudge to move the needles until the red chip disappears (undo and re-roll with Brute Spin or nudges), or defend with block. Hover the LETHAL tag to see why (a staged card can turn a Corrupted slice into a killing hit). Spamming SEND IT at LETHAL got Breakers killed.

Don't enter fights at low HP: HP carries over, healing is scarce, and Breakers arriving at 2-28 HP repeatedly flatlined within a few turns, especially against elites, the 45 HP Triage Unit, the 40 HP Collections Agent and the 112 HP Claims Adjuster (2 HP flatlined turn 1). Defend or heal rather than just sending. A 2 HP win over Triage with Guard was possible but rare.

Enemy resistance absorbs one tick per point before the wheel moves, so you cannot just spin past it; count the nudges a resisted wheel needs. Flip (Mirror Flip) and Respin are blocked while resistance (or Guard) is up; Jam nudges \u00b11 and ignores resistance, and Jolt can lower resist.
Undo is blocked after a random event or a respin (or random pick/draw, or a Jolt that triggers one), and any RAM debt then persists, so commit to a plan before triggering those.
A "lethal" preview against a healing or blocking enemy can be false, so expect heal and block to eat part of the damage and don't rely on the number alone.
A turn that drops both sides to 0 HP counts as a defeat: the fight is lost even if the enemy shows DELETED.

Read the preview and the needle position each turn: sending without playing cards when the needle lands on a good slice saves RAM, and a natural landing on your biggest slice can finish a fight. An enemy needle on its block slice gives a breather turn.

The needle slice you land on sets the outcome (Perfect/Good/Weak/Null); aim for your big overflow 12 slice, since most damage comes from it (Perfect 12 hits hardest, doubling damage e.g. 24, and can win a fight in about 5 turns; NULL does nothing, Weak 12 is poor); use the free nudge, Fine Tune, Jolt, Brute Spin or a Respin to move it there. Perfect is the dead centre of a slice.
Respin (4 RAM, random result) is worth paying for when the needle is stuck on a null or low slice; it once produced a 12 slice. It makes Undo unavailable.

Enemy wheels can have block slices (e.g. a 14 block) that absorb your attack, and Guard adds block that absorbs hit damage, so check what the enemy needle sits on and read the preview before attacking.

Check where the enemy's pointer sits before spinning its wheel or sending; a spin can land it on a big attack slice such as 14 or 15 (Overflow 15 flagged lethal on Recall Unit), and enemy Perfect slices hit hard (Dispenser Perfect 6 left a Breaker at 1 HP). Nudge or Jolt big enemy spikes (like the Collections Agent 14) away from the needle. Jolt/spin cards can also hurt your own Breaker, so read damage to you.

Early fights can take 10+ turns (Triage fights up to ~20, tutorial fights ~11 and can drain 44-59 HP; a first Billing Daemon fight (42 HP) took 13-18 turns, Collections Agent 16), with several turns of spins landing on block and no damage dealt, so plan for long attrition; some fights end in 4-5 turns when a kill preview is lined up. HP carries over between tutorial fights.

Mashing the same card and Send It without engaging the wheels or reading the enemy wheel costs lots of HP (a Collections Agent fight cost 50 HP, Billing Daemon 52) and drags fights out; read the enemy wheel and your options each turn.

Healer enemies like Triage Unit regenerate about 3-8 per turn (it went 7/45 back to 25/45; HP+3/HP+6 slices) and block small slices, so burst them on a big slice (12+; Jolt or Brute Spin can rotate them off block/heal) rather than chipping. Hotfix heals the enemy 6, so avoid it.
A PERFECT landing is a rare bonus (0-1 per fight), so don't rely on it.
Wheel colours: red is damage, blue is shields, green is RAM and statuses.

Cards can be overspent; the shortfall shows as a negative RAM debt chip (hatched segment) that can persist across turns (-5/-6 on turn 1 made a 4 RAM respin unaffordable), and overdrawing RAM preceded lost fights (though in one case RAM was back to 12/12 next turn). Respin costs 4 RAM, rerolls the wheel and cleared one debt. Queued cards stack the debt, so watch the total before queuing several.

Check the RAM counter before playing a card; a card that costs more RAM than you have is refused (shows NEED cost) and a red 'Not enough RAM' banner explains why (this can look like a targeting failure). Mirror Flip (3 RAM) is unplayable at low RAM; Brute Spin needs 2. RAM (12 per turn) pays for cards, respins and extra nudges and refills each turn.
Fights can start with only 6/12 RAM on turn 1, so plan the opening turn around about half RAM.

Use the free nudge each turn before Send It and before spending RAM on cards; it is one free tick per turn and the counter shows how many remain (a turn may show none). It can fail to help if it lands on a NULL slice. Extra nudges cost 1 RAM.
Check the incoming-damage badge on your HP each turn and prioritise defence or Mirror Flip when it threatens lethal; Mirror Flip turned a -24 incoming preview into -9.
Enemies' 1/0 dud slices mean little or no incoming damage, so those turns are safe windows to attack or skip cards.

Enemy slices apply effects such as Shim damage or Dose (applies CORRUPTED or a drain to your wheel); hover slices and pointers to read them. NULL slices do nothing unless a Daemon says otherwise. Enemies can also carry Guard (Triage 45) and show Perfect markers and Blocked/Guard values; some are tagged 'Weak to Good'.
You win by bringing the enemy's HP to 0; if the Breaker's HP hits 0 the fight is lost and that Breaker is permanently killed and the netrun fails, so treat Breaker HP as the run's lifeline.
Cards can be left in the tray or queued across a turn, and RAM regenerates between turns, so unspent cheap cards carry value into the next turn.

A negative number beside the RAM counter, with a hatched pink pip, is RAM committed or debt (queued cards show a negative total like -8); it also appears as the price of a selected card (e.g. (-3) for Jolt), can persist for many turns then vanish, and is not explained on screen.
Conserve HP early, since the map offered no heal between several straight fights and HP carries over; keep defensive cards.

Precision tags: PERFECT is best output (dead centre), GOOD is full output on its slice, WEAK is half, NULL does nothing. A GOOD tag on an enemy pointer is a real hit coming at you. Tags are not defined on screen but the PRECISION TAG tooltip explains them; judge from preview numbers.
Wheels move on their own each turn (each turn begins with a random spin, which locks Undo), and the free nudge at turn start is a chance to adjust them before SEND IT.

Overdrive costs 1 RAM, multiplies the pointer slice by 1.5x on its next trigger, then makes it CORRUPTED (-1 RAM, 3 self-damage per Major Heat threshold), so use it only when a single big hit is worth it and avoid it at low HP. Sanitize counters the penalty.

Fights reward Cycles (about 15-25) and a pick of one of three cards (or skip), and some fights also offer a Firmware chip such as Patch+ (+50% slice output) versus Shunt, Bulkhead, Siphon or Barbed Wire; node previews say when a chip is possible. Read both before choosing. Picked rewards do apply even though the screen jumps straight on.
On loot sheets you may skip to keep the deck lean; prefer cards usable on your wheel, since inner-ring or corruption-based cards can be dead picks. Space auto-takes card 1.
Don't take inner-ring cards such as Inner Drift, Inner Snap, Ring Tap or Gear Shift if the target wheel has no inner ring; they are dead cards ('Target has no inner ring').
Pick healing cards like Patch Up in loot when HP is low and keep one in hand for later fights.

Firmware chips only install on a matching slice type; Siphon and Static Coat were rejected on an OVERFLOW slice ('does not fit', shown only after you try), so check compatibility and try another slot or chip (e.g. Hardened, Shunt) or Continue stays blocked.

Firmware chips like Patch+ raise a slice's value (the 12 slice became 18), Shunt resolves the neighbour slice on a Perfect only, Bulkhead boosts DEFRAG/SANDBOX output, and the wheel preview shows where the chip will land before you socket it. Patch+ on the OVFL 12 slot makes your main damage slice hit harder.
The game chooses the firmware slot, so two offers aimed at the same slot (Patch+ and Bulkhead both on Slot 1) compete; take the one that fits your build.
Cards cost RAM, with a budget of 12 per turn that refills each turn, shown in the RAM readout (bottom-left) and dropping by the cost when you stage a card.
Higher-cost cards like Mirror Flip (3 RAM) and Brute Spin (2 RAM) may be unplayable early, so spend RAM on cheap cards first and plan the turn around the cost.

Card basics: Jolt is a cheap random rotation of 3 ticks clockwise (a couple of Jolts often reach the 12 slice but it can miss), Brute Spin 6 ticks for 2 RAM (some saw 3-4), Fine Tune is two \u00b11 nudges on one ring for 1-2 RAM (cheap precise option, awkward to aim), Mirror Flip flips a wheel (3 RAM; blocked while the target has resistance or Guard; can be aimed at an enemy wheel), Jam nudges an enemy wheel ignoring resistance, Snap (2 RAM) snaps the needle to slice centre, Data Surge draws 3, Nudge Driver makes nudge cards trigger twice. Brute Spin was one tester's main damage card. Right-click a card to read its tooltip first.
Mirror Flip on the enemy wheel can cut an incoming hit sharply (GOOD 16 to GOOD 8; Recall Unit preview 16/1 to 16/4), a useful defensive play.
Fine Tune and nudge-type cards can have their aim arc land on the enemy's nudge arrow instead of your wheel; verify the target in the preview.
Clicking a wheel in Brute Spin aim mode may queue multiple spins without visible turning; check RAM and the THIS TURN list, then undo before a random event locks it.
Brute Spin is useless on a wheel of mostly small equal slices (e.g. 6 slices) because it just goes a full lap.
Cards that rotate or alter wheels (Fine Tune, Hub Breach, Mirror Flip) move a lethal slice away from the needle, but Mirror Flip was refused on a Daemon wheel with a lockdown hub, with no message.
Freeze applies a FROZEN tag to the enemy but will not save you from heavy incoming damage when your HP is low; it may not cancel the hit shown in the incoming preview.
Block cards like Firewall (6 block) are worth playing when low on HP, but alone they do not beat an elite at low HP.
Sanitize only removes CORRUPTED cards or slices and gives 3 block, so it is a dead pick when nothing is corrupted.
Armour-style cards like Strip, which reduce enemy resistance, may help against resistant enemies (effect unconfirmed).
The number on cards like Mirror Flip is RAM cost; Heat did not change when it was played.

HP carries between fights with no healing on the route map (only the run's end heals fully), so avoid taking big damage early; entering later nodes at low HP is very dangerous (one Breaker went 60\u219210\u21927 and died at L4; others went 60\u219225\u219213, 60\u219223\u21928\u21922 or 60\u219216 over three fights). The map often offers a single forced next node. Look for heal events, a Rack route or a Terminal.

Elite fights (about 106-112 HP: Claims Adjuster, Recall Unit) are very dangerous for a Breaker below about 30 HP; take the plain fight instead when a choice exists. At low HP the route can leave only an Elite on layer 3 (13/60, 16/60 and 19/60 all lost), so arrive with HP in reserve and block cards; heal first when you see an Elite coming.

Do not enter a Rack node (extra Schematics, +2 Heat, a 112 HP enemy such as Claims Adjuster, a long fight) at low HP; it can end the run. Routes can force a Rack as the only next node, so keep HP in reserve (forced Racks at 16/60, 11/60, 9 and 6 HP killed runs).

Event nodes can heal or cut Heat: Wellness Kiosk gives about +10 HP (once also raised max HP) for +2 Heat (its Jam option costs -3 HP and is greyed out at very low HP), Patient Records gives -2 Heat for -5 HP. But an event node can turn out to be a fight, and some free-looking options lead to one.

Event option costs are shown as chips, and you cannot pay a cost you cannot afford (e.g. -12 HP or -60 Cycles); pick the free option. Locked Ward costs 12 HP or 60 Cycles to rescue an operative; Ghost past is free but gives nothing.
Check the route tooltip before choosing a node: two fights with identical follow-ups are equivalent because the enemy is rolled on entry.

Hover route-map nodes (or read the sidebar/route panel, e.g. '[1] Fight > Rack') to see type, tier, rewards and Heat cost, such as Elite (+1 Heat, Firmware), Rack (+2 Heat) or T1 fights paying 15-25 Cycles, and check them before choosing. Orange-ringed circles are the nodes you can walk to; the bottom legend decodes icons.
On the route map, click a node first, then confirm with CONFIRM or Enter; clicking a node alone does not confirm it and CONFIRM stays greyed until one is picked.

On the campaign map, select a site (its panel shows what it opens; the orange ring marks the next one) then press JACK IN (let the animation finish), which starts a netrun with your first ready Breaker; routes are then chosen layer by layer showing Fight, RACK and SHOP nodes. The opening site is Continuum Billing Farm (T1); clearing it opens Pricing Memo Archive and Scrub Records.

Sites on the city grid are gated (a Clear First ring): hover or select a locked site to read which site must be cleared first (e.g. Central Server needs a linked Site; Patient Records Vault needs the Billing Farm); clicking a locked node does nothing else, so don't re-click it.
The legend lists RACK as healing, but other sessions saw no heal at Racks (they bank and cost Heat); don't count on a Rack to heal.
Fights pay about 18-22 Cycles each, and Cycles accumulate in the wallet.
Shop prices start around 50+ cycles (cards 50-72, slices 100), so early wallets (~39-42) can't afford anything and the shop offers no healing; save before visiting or skip it.

The Market sells next-run boosts with Schematics (Warm Cache 10 gives 40 starting Cycles, Overclocked Deck 15, Field Kit 20), a Breaker recruit for 15 and class unlocks (Bunker 40, Hivemind 60, Botnet/Ghost/Fortress 80); hover to confirm effects. The charge is taken when you queue the item.
Heat Scrub costs 25 Schematics (-5 Heat) at the Core, so save Schematics for it; it can't be used with only 10.
A Locked Ward terminal costs 60 cycles to rescue an operative.
Keep Schematics banked: with only 5 you cannot recruit (15; a 'Not enough Schematics' toast appears) or buy boosts, though after a wipe a recruit can cost 0 even if the card shows 15.
A flatline (losing a fight) loses the run's cycles and unbanked loot; banked Schematics are kept.
RAM is the per-turn resource for card plays and Respin; budget it each turn (a turn can end at 0 RAM after spends).
Bank Schematics at the Cell/Rack early and never jack out with unbanked loot (it is lost); banking cools Heat per the tooltip (one session saw Racks add Heat), but high Heat brings raids.
A Rack is a fight then a bank, costs +2 Heat, and the enemy has far more HP (112) than normal fights (38-45).
Elite nodes add Heat (+1) but give Firmware rewards.

Each flatline adds about +11-14 Heat plus a few per node cleared; a raider reaching CORE adds more, and a raid itself adds Heat (+5). Heat accumulates across flatlines (11, 22, 25+, 30>42>53) and crossing a threshold triggers a raid. Events (kiosk) add Heat too.

Heat thresholds trigger raids from Collections (about 25-30, 50-57, 75) and effects like Elite Frequency +25% at 38; Heat 30 (Noticed) means the next Mainframe carries one fewer item, ~52 is Flagged. Hover the Heat counter for the next threshold; Heat is a 0-100 hunt meter with a first threshold at 10.
Heat 80 did not end the campaign in one session: the bar runs to 100 (HUNTED) and HQ continued at Heat 81 and 86.
High Heat (e.g. 70) adds a '+1 RESISTANCE' modifier to enemies, making fights harder.
MAJOR Heat thresholds make Corrupted cost 3 self-damage per threshold, so Heat can hurt you in combat.
Normal fights did not raise Heat in the first site (it stayed 0 through three fights, and a new netrun starts at 0); per-card Heat isn't shown.

To lower Heat, clear Heat-reduction sites (Scrub Records, Purge Camera Logs, Wipe Biometrics, Burn the Ledger; all locked behind other sites, so clear early sites first) or pay Heat Scrub (25 Schematics, -5 Heat, key H).

A raid with no crew or armory still plays out and costs Home HP and adds Heat (50>40, then 40>27 or 32, 50>38, Heat 25>30, 33>38, 53>58; one raid cost Home -29); raid setup shows the stakes and crew ready.
Raid Setup's projection (e.g. Core 50>40 HOLDS, 'IF THE RAID RUNS NOW HOME -10') matched the playout result exactly, so it can be trusted; check it after every change.
Spend Schematics on PATCH (+5 CORE integrity, found in the Crew tab) before a raid; it turned a projected BREACHED (27>0) into HOLDS (34>5).
The raid report ends with BACK TO THE GRID, which needs a mouse click; Enter and Esc do nothing.
A raid with every Breaker flatlined can breach HQ and end the campaign, so keep at least one operative alive or recruited before a raid (a raid with Crew 0/4 still ran and damaged Home).
Press R at HQ to open Raid Setup when a raid is incoming; START DEFENSE needs a mouse click.
The Defence armory (0/6) fills only from assets banked by runs, so you can't prepare raid defence from HQ alone.
CORE is your home server: you defend it in raids and never run it.

Breaker death is permanent: you lose the run's cycles, gain Heat (+11), and return to HQ via Back to HQ; Schematics and Home are kept. HQ has no revive or rest option (the map text says to recruit or rest at HQ but no button exists; use the MARKET). Jack in with the next crew member at full HP; with zero ready crew Jack In is blocked. A flatline can queue a raid.
Recruit Breakers in the HQ Market tab, not Crew (the CREW tab did nothing); after a total wipe the first recruit costs 0 Schematics, later ones 15.
The win condition is collecting 3 Exploits from gold Exploit Sites to open the Central Server (Genome Core); you start with two Breakers.

HQ sites are chained and locked behind prerequisites (start with the open T1 site, Continuum Billing Farm); the first runnable site has an orange ring. Open the MAP KEY (explains rings) and look/pan to the far left rather than clicking locked sites.
The Relay Nest server is locked behind 50 Schematics (bought in the Black Market), so unlock it through campaign progress.

New Campaign setup has locked targets, servers and crew that need unlock counts (targets 120-160, crew 60-80); only Solace Biosystems, Standard and Breaker are unlocked at first (Hivemind needs UNLOCKS 60). A fresh campaign starts with 2 READY Breakers. Today's Run and Share Codes sit below the start controls.
The crew can hold more than two Breakers and flatlined ones do not block ready ones: check the crew panel (e.g. Breakers 3 and 4 READY) before assuming the run is over; keep spare Breakers ready.

The campaign autosaves; Save & Quit (or quitting, including to desktop or mid-fight via the pause menu) stores it and Continue/BREACH on the title resumes it at the same route node with HP, Heat and wallet. Save & Quit may need repeated clicks to show, and is on the run map rather than the pause menu in one build view. Quit to Desktop's Save & Quit confirm was unresponsive in one session.
Patch on the HQ crew panel costs 5 Schematics for +5 integrity on CORE only; it does not revive Breakers.
The CREW button can read 0/2 and be unresponsive when no breaker is ready, and the CORE panel can capture map clicks.

Read card text and rules by hovering or right-clicking the card, because the on-card text is truncated and tooltips (not the tutorial or banners) explain nudge, targeting and costs. Hover bars, chips, the SEND IT button and wheel pointers (Heat bar, RAM, Shim, Overflow) too; the Codex Slices entry has full slice text.
Hover the RAM bar for its explanation: RAM pays for cards, respins and extra nudges, and refills each turn.
A negative RAM figure beside the bar (e.g. (-2)) appeared during fights and while aiming, and cleared when an enemy fell, after Undo, or after several turns; the game never explained it.

The tutorial/training sim win screen and FIGHT WON banner show no Continue prompt and clicks or Enter do nothing; open the gear-icon pause menu (or Esc) and Quit to Main Menu to leave, and the tutorial saves no campaign. If the Finish button looks disabled, use Skip tutorial.

Some screens do show key hints: the loot/result footer shows Space as next step, Raid Setup is [R], Heat Scrub is [H], RESUME is [Esc], and the quit confirm shows Save & Quit [A] / Keep Going [B] (though A did not work). SEND IT [Space] appeared only once the turn's cards were set.
Red numbers on the HP bars are last turn's SEND IT HP change; hover to confirm.
The Codex (214 entries, Slices and Lexicon tabs) is reachable from the pause menu and has no search, how-to-play page or entry defining 'nudge'; hover tooltips are the faster source for basic rules.
Open the MAP KEY button (top right) to learn node icons (next, cleared, yours, down, taken, heat objective, locked, exploit); it has no HQ entry.
Read the side panel or tooltip of a locked site to learn its gate instead of re-clicking it; selecting a site on the HQ map shows what gates it.
Overlapping cards in hand make it easy to select the wrong one, so confirm the selection through the wheel chips or tooltip before spending RAM.

The pause menu (Resume [Esc], Options, Codex, Quit to Main Menu, Quit to Desktop; shows a Campaign code) places Abandon Run/Campaign ('No Going Back', no confirm step in one session) right next to Resume and Quit, so click carefully; it has no retry (after a tutorial loss, quit to menu and re-enter). Quitting autosaves and the title then offers CONTINUE. On the HQ map it may only open after clicking the bottom-left area first.

Raise the text scale slider (1.0-2.0x) in Options > Accessibility only if needed, because at 2.0x setup screens need lots of scrolling and START is hard to find; other options include reduce effects, colour-blind modes and high contrast.
The tutorial overlay can reappear on later fights and its step 4/7 box can block the board until Space is pressed.
The first netrun tutorial box is the only explanation of wheels, RAM, resistance and banking; skipping it left a tester confused, so read it.
Nudge Driver gives two free nudges (nudge cards trigger twice next turn), which helps line up wheels cheaply.
Firmware offers can include healing like Siphon (heal 2 on Good+), though it may not fit the OVERFLOW slot.
